items.title: Three rescued, woman missing in Ipoh water surge
items.summary: IPOH: A 21-year-old woman is feared drowned after being swept away by strong currents during a sudden surge of water at Puncak Jelapang Waterfall in Meru Raya today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Meru Raya fire and rescue station was dispatched to the scene, 10km away, after receiving an emergency call at 5.14pm. Sabarodzi said the search and rescue operation was focused on locating the missing woman, but the water current remained strong.

items.title: Cardiothoracic services at Johor hospital unaffected despite department head's resignation
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Cardiothoracic services at Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) remain unaffected and are operating as usual following the resignation of the department head on Monday. HSA director Dr Mohamad Nizam Subahir said the cardiothoracic team continued to provide services in accordance with established clinical requirements. "However, the resignation does not affect the continuity of cardiothoracic services to patients," he said in a statement.

items.title: Indonesia foils attempts to smuggle 25.8kg of gold to Malaysia this month
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian customs authorities have foiled three attempts this month to smuggle 25.8kg of gold worth an estimated 62.5 billion rupiah (RM14.06 million) to Malaysia. Teluk Bayur Customs and Excise Office head Ade Zirwan said the 34-year-old was detained at Minangkabau International Airport near Padang, West Sumatra, on Nov 12 for attempting to smuggle 4kg of gold worth an estimated 10 billion rupiah (RM2.25 million) out of Indonesia. In a separate statement, Indonesia's Directorate General of Customs and Excise said officers seized another 21.8 kilogrammes of gold worth an estimated 52.5 billion rupiah (RM11.80 million) in two cases involving passengers departing from Syamsudin Noor International Airport near Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, on Nov 5 and 12.

items.title: Mascot-mad fans flock to meet-up of 200 characters in Japan
items.summary: HANYU: Tens of thousands of mascot fans gathered in a city near Tokyo on Saturday to meet and greet more than 200 life-size cuddly characters promoting local towns and businesses. The mascot meet-up has been held in the city of Hanyu since 2010, and nearly 220 mascots were invited to join this year, according to organisers. "These local mascot characters representing regions are part of Japanese culture.

items.title: Maritime agency says two tankers struck in Hormuz as Iran says ship on fire
items.summary: DUBAI: Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, British maritime agency UKMTO said, as Iran reported that a ship was on fire. Iran's army on Saturday said a ship was on fire after hitting a mine in the strait. "Before noon today, a violating oil tanker that had entered a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after striking a naval mine," Iran's army naval forces said in a statement carried by state TV.

items.title: Negri Sembilan police yet to receive report from MB over resignation letter
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan police have yet to receive a report from Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim over an alleged resignation letter submitted to the palace without his knowledge or consent. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that Ismail had not lodged a police report so far. Earlier today, Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin confirmed receiving a report over allegations that a letter of resignation by the Negri Sembilan menteri besar was submitted to the palace without his consent.

items.title: Wife of firefighter missing in Nepal harassed by debt collectors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of a senior fire officer reported missing in Nepal has spoken of the distress caused by repeated calls and threats from parties seeking to recover her husband's debts. Hani Othman, 40, said she first received calls from an e-commerce platform company in October informing her that her husband, Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, had outstanding payments. She said the calls had become increasingly frequent, with more than 10 calls a day from the parties involved.

items.title: 159 longhouse residents receive food aid as floods submerge ground floor
items.summary: KUCHING: A total of 159 residents of a longhouse in the interior of Kapit received food supplies from firefighters after floodwaters submerged its entire ground floor to a depth of more than 2m today. The 27-door John Kara longhouse in Kerangan was inundated, forcing residents to take shelter on the upper floor for their safety. He said a team from the Kapit Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to monitor the situation and deliver food supplies to the affected residents.

items.title: Flood situation improves in Perak, Selangor; Negri Sembilan fully recovers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Perak and Selangor fell to 2,334 people from 683 families this afternoon, down from 2,368 people from 691 families this morning. However, SK Tanjung Belanja remains open, sheltering 70 evacuees from 35 families. In Kerian, 180 evacuees from 57 families, including 12 people from three families affected by a landslide, remain at SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman.

items.title: PKR open to PH parties using own logos in GE16
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: PKR is not ruling out the possibility of Pakatan Harapan (PH) component parties using their respective logos in the 16th General Election (GE16), saying the proposal warrants consideration by the coalition's top leadership. Kamil was responding to a proposal for PH component parties, including PKR, DAP and Amanah, to use their respective logos in the next general election instead of a single coalition logo. "Indeed, the PKR logo made history when it helped PH win the 2018 general election," he said.

items.title: Trump threatens to tax US firms that build data centres abroad
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose a steep tax on US companies that build data centres overseas. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," Trump told reporters at a White House briefing, reported German news agency dpa. US companies have been building data centres abroad, including in Europe, for years.

items.title: South Korean president reiterates US$75,000 reward for reporting college exam cheating
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reiterated on Saturday that the government would offer a reward of 100 million won (US$75,000) to anyone reporting cases of cheating in this week's college entrance examination, describing the misconduct as a "crime as serious as corruption" involving government officials, Yonhap News Agency reported. Lee made the comments on social media, saying the reward would be paid for each case of cheating reported. "Cheating on the college entrance exam is a crime as serious as corruption by public officials," Lee said.

items.title: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes Banda Sea near Timor-Leste
items.summary: BENGALURU: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Banda Sea, 226km north-east of Dili, Timor-Leste on Saturday, the German Research Center for Geosciences (GFZ) said. The quake was at a depth of 117km, GFZ said. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Cooperation with Thailand helps keep drugs out of Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: Kelantan police have maintained close cooperation with their Thai counterparts to curb cross-border criminal activities, particularly drug smuggling. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cooperation had helped prevent prohibited substances, especially drugs, from entering the country through the state. He said Thai authorities had also stepped up border security and planned to establish more checkpoints to tackle cross-border crime.

items.title: PN sees BN as most suitable partner for GE16
items.summary: KUANTAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) appears to be the most suitable partner for Perikatan Nasional (PN), based on their electoral cooperation in Negri Sembilan and Melaka. Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah said the cooperation, dubbed the "Blue Wave", appeared to be gaining traction, particularly in the Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections. The BN-PN cooperation secured a two-thirds majority in the Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections.

items.title: Perhilitan to set up camera traps to detect black panther in Sendayan
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) will install camera traps to detect a black panther after residents reported sightings in the Laman Sendayan residential area. Its director, Wan Mat Wan Harun, said the move is to verify the complaint's authenticity before taking further action. "We received the report around 2pm today, and our team will set up camera traps this evening," he told Bernama here today.

items.title: Missing MCKK student found safe
items.summary: IPOH: A 13-year-old Malay College Kuala Kangsar (MCKK) student who was reported missing yesterday was found safe in Taiping, four hours after police received a report on the disappearance. Kuala Kangsar police chief Assistant Commissioner Heisham Harun said police received a report from the student's mother around 6pm after she was informed by the school that her child was missing. Earlier, a post went viral on social media about a Form One student from a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar who had been missing since yesterday.

items.title: Four teens held after police chase near Simpang Pulai
items.summary: Tapah deputy police chief deputy superintendent Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of policemen on patrol received information at 4.20pm from the district police headquarters control centre to assist Ringlet station personnel in tracking down a Toyota Chery multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several people suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case. "Police then chased the vehicle to the Tapah toll plaza. Fadzil said personnel from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined the chase before police intercepted the vehicle at Simpang Pulai.

items.title: 25pc surge in patients causes congestion at Ampang Hospital
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A surge of up to 25 per cent above the daily average in patients seeking treatment at the Yellow Zone of Ampang Hospital's Emergency and Trauma Department has caused congestion and prolonged waiting times for ward admission. The Selangor Health Department said the recent increase in patient numbers had also affected the smooth processing of admissions to the hospital's wards. The department said Ampang Hospital's management introduced several measures to address the congestion following the surge in patients.

items.title: No fake work pass syndicates detected in Kelantan, other border states
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Immigration Department has yet to detect any syndicates producing or distributing fake Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) in Kelantan or other states bordering Thailand. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said investigations so far had uncovered cases only in the Klang Valley. On Wednesday, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah told the Dewan Rakyat that 36 Immigration Department officers and personnel had been detained, suspended or charged over a syndicate allegedly involved in issuing fake documents and Temporary Employment Visit Passes since 2025.

items.title: Malaysian man caught with 4kg gold hidden in shoes at Indonesian airport
items.summary: Teluk Bayur Customs Office chief Ade Zirwan said the inspection was conducted with the assistance of airport security personnel. Ade said the inspection uncovered four gold bars hidden in the man's shoes, with two bars concealed in each shoe. He said the gold was estimated to be worth 10 billion rupiah (about RM2.25 million).

items.title: MOE studying need for more assistant wardens, counselling teachers
items.summary: Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children's own abilities and emotional readiness. Our dreams as parents must align with our children's own abilities and emotional readiness," she said in a Facebook post today. The discussions covered compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs), hostel management, and the importance of parents assessing their children's level of readiness before sending them to boarding schools.

items.title: Mother devastated after losing two children in Sik fire
items.summary: SIK: A 23-year-old mother was left devastated after her two children died in a fire at a former office building converted into a home in Kampung Teloi Tua here today. The children were found dead on a bed inside the premises. Police investigations found that the children had been living with their unemployed mother at their grandfather's home.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Saturday, Nov 21, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1582644]] [[nid:1582643]] [[nid:1582642]] [[nid:1582641]] [[nid:1582640]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Family escapes injury as car crashes into power pole, damaging house
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A family escaped injury after a car crashed into a power pole outside their home in Bandar Permas Jaya here, causing the pole to fall onto the roof and damage part of the house. "I cannot imagine what would have happened to my family if the power pole had fallen on the bedroom," he said. The chicken rice seller said his family was asleep when the incident occurred about 2am today.

items.title: Legal certainty key to public confidence in judiciary - Chief Justice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Legal certainty is essential to maintaining public confidence in the judiciary, as citizens must be able to rely on the law when navigating legal matters and making decisions, said Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh. He said legal certainty was important because everyone appearing before a Malaysian court needed absolute clarity on what the law dictates and whether they could rely on it. Underscoring the importance of legal certainty, Justice Wan Ahmad Farid said it affected everyone, including investors, businesses, ordinary citizens, and accused persons, who required clarity on what the law dictated and whether it could be relied upon.

items.title: Air Niugini flight lands safely in Philippines after emergency
items.summary: MANILA: An Air Niugini plane carrying 146 passengers and crew from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea made an emergency landing safely on Saturday in a southern Philippine city after an indication of a possible engine fire, Philippine aviation officials said. There were no reports of injuries among the 137 passengers and nine crew members, who disembarked using emergency slides from the Boeing 767-383ER after it diverted from its route and landed at Davao International Airport, the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines said, according to AP. They followed safety procedures and requested an unscheduled landing in Davao shortly after midnight, Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines spokesperson Eric Apolonio said, without elaborating.

items.title: MCA leaves Negri Sembilan crisis decisions to BN leadership
items.summary: MCA deputy president Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the party had not issued any specific instructions to its assemblymen so far. Meanwhile, in his speech at the assembly, Mah said MCA's cooperation with other parties should be assessed pragmatically. "Therefore, the strategic cooperation of other parties, including MCA, must also be judged by the same standards," he said.

items.title: Armizan: GRS to decide GE16 direction collectively
items.summary: PAPAR: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) has yet to decide on the form of political cooperation for the 16th general election (GE16) and the matter has been left to the coalition's Supreme Council to discuss and decide upon collectively when the time is right. GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said any decision must take into account the views of component parties which reflect the voices of members at the grassroots as well as the signals sent by the public during the 2025 Sabah state election. However, he said, GRS is open to political cooperation drawing on the coalition's past experience of working with other parties, both before and after the previous Sabah state election, to ensure the stability of the state administration.

items.title: Sabah community-based tourism generates RM7mil in 2025
items.summary: Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the figures reflected its potential to generate income for communities and support the rural economy. He said the state aimed to ensure that all registered community-based tourism and homestay products in Sabah met the relevant Asean standards by 2030. Sabah currently has 13 community tourism and homestay products listed under the Asean tourism standard awards, covering community-based tourism, homestays and sustainable tourism.

items.title: First ECRL ride? It’s your chance to explore some East Coast attractions and sample some great local eats
items.summary: KotaSAS The first major stop is KotaSAS Station in Pahang, located approximately eight kilometres from Indera Mahkota, a suburb of Kuantan, and 10 kilometres from the city centre. Teluk Cempedak is a popular beach located approximately five kilometres east of Kuantan city centre and about 15 kilometres from KotaSAS Station. Kuala Terengganu The second major stop is Kuala Terengganu Station in Terengganu, approximately 8.7 kilometres from Bukit Payong, a suburb of Kuala Terengganu and 23 kilometres from the city centre.

items.title: Accountant finds stress relief in origami, turns 1,111 paper folds into eye-catching 3D arch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Spending her days immersed in figures and financial statements has not stopped an accountant from expressing her creative side through the art of paper folding, or origami, with her three-dimensional (3D) craft creations attracting considerable attention. What began as a way to relax has since evolved into something more remarkable, with the 45-year-old successfully creating a 3D origami arch using 1,111 origami units, showcasing how the art form can be transformed into unique and creative decorative pieces. Known as the Kusudama Arch, the creation, made using the Kusudama Sonobe technique and comprising 38 paper balls of various sizes and 151 heart-shaped ornaments, attracted visitors’ attention during the World Origami Day celebration held here recently.

items.title: From factory floor to AI, Micron Malaysia employees chart career paths through skills development
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — From starting as an operator to training others, and from working in component assembly to exploring artificial intelligence (AI), employees at Micron Malaysia are building their skills and advancing their careers as manufacturing processes become increasingly sophisticated. Nor Shamim Mat Saffar, who joined Micron as an operator in 2019, has completed Levels 2 and 3 of the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and progressed to training others. Her initial work in surface mount technology front-of-line operations provided a foundation in manufacturing, safety, quality and adherence to standard operating procedures.

items.title: Kedah records 406 fatal motorcycle accidents in 10 months, 72 involving under-18 riders
items.summary: Kedah police contingent headquarters (IPK) Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief, Superintendent Abdel Nasser S. Salleh, said these statistics indicate that the safety of motorcyclists particularly teenagers requires serious attention. “Seized motorcycles may be reclaimed, subject to compliance with stipulated terms and procedures including replacing non-compliant components with original parts or approved standard components,” he said in a statement here today. Abdel Nasser said enforcement efforts will continue to be intensified to ensure that road users adhere to established laws and regulations.

items.title: Man who posed as Selangor royal aide gets 27 more months’ jail, two strokes of cane for vehicle scam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A man who impersonated an Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the Raja Muda of Selangor and had been sentenced to imprisonment for fraud involving property and luxury vehicle purchases was sentenced to another 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane today for similar offences. Today, Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was sentenced by the Magistrate’s Court here to a total of 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for cheating two victims of RM73,000 in a vehicle auction scam. Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin meted out the jail sentence and fine after Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty to the charges.

items.title: Police seize RM1.27m in health, cosmetic and food products in Banting raid, three held
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — Police detained three individuals and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million during a raid at a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor yesterday. He said checks found 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of pure tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products and various tea-based food and beverage items and snacks. In the same operation, the Kuala Langat District Health Office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500.

items.title: Lorry driver in Sabah to face trial in April 2027 over alleged sexual offence against stepdaughter, 16
items.summary: Sessions Court Judge Zaini Fishir set the date for the man whose case was brought up for pre-trial case management to serve all the relevant documents. The court had released the man on bail of RM10,000 with RM5,000 deposited in two local sureties after granting his application of bail through his counsel. Earlier, counsel Jagnesh Jaya who defended the man, applied for bail to be granted as in previous proceedings in Tuaran Sessions Court, the man was not granted bail.

items.title: ‘Qibla marker’ on Mount Kinabalu is a prayer aid, not a religious privilege, says Sabah mufti
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — The provision of a qibla (direction of prayer) marker on Mount Kinabalu is a basic facility for Muslims to perform prayers and is not intended to grant exclusive rights to any religion, said Sabah Mufti Datuk Dr Bungsu @ Aziz Jaafar. “The presence of the qibla marker does not in any way prevent followers of other religions from praying or practising their respective faiths on the mountain. “There is no such thing as exclusive privileges for any particular religion on Mount Kinabalu,” he said, adding that anyone could engage in religious activities, subject to their needs and approval from Sabah Parks.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB disowns resignation letter submitted to Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has clarified that he never authorised the submission of his resignation letter to Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, contrary to reports on Monday. Earlier, Ismail was granted an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap, which was also attended by Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi. Following the audience, Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, said Tuanku Muhriz had decreed that he continue serving as Menteri Besar to ensure continuity in the state administration.

items.title: Four years’ jail, counselling and police supervision for Sabah pensioner , 69, convicted of child sex offence
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — A 69-year-old pensioner was sentenced to four years’ jail for committing sexual physical harassment against a minor.Sessions Court Judge Noor Hafizah Mohd Noor imposed the sentence to Jamran Abdul Majit after ruling that the prosecution had proven its case beyond reasonable doubt against Jamran.He was found guilty of committing the sexual abuse on the 10-year and eight-month-old girl by touching the victim’s breast, stomach and grabbed the victim’s private part at 3pm on July 18, 2024, inside a shop in Manggatal, here.Jamran was convicted under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.Jamran was ordered to undergo rehabilitative counseling while serving the jail sentence and to be placed under police supervision for three years after completing the jail term.The court ordered Jamran to serve the jail sentence from the date of his conviction on Thursday.However, the court granted Jamran’s application to stay execution pending appeal against the decision to the High Court and released on the same bail and conditions as previous one.Six prosecution and two defence witnesses had testified in the hearing.During mitigation, counsels Mohamad Syazwan Shah together Nigel Neong Kaning who defended Jamran, asked for a minimum sentence saying that Jamran was a pensioner and has a wife who is depending on him.Syazwan told the court that Jamran was also suffering from several medical conditions such as thyroid, cholesterol, prostrate having problem, severe back pain and currently receiving treatment from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital 2 and Manggatal Health Clinic.He also added that it was Jamran’s first offence.However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir who conducted the prosecution, urged the court to impose a heavy sentence on Jamran in the grounds that it was a serious offence.Fazriel submitted that it was in the public interest that children are protected from sexual predators, especially within the same living area. “The court must send a clear message that such conduct will be met with severe consequences. “In light of the foregoing aggravating factors particularly the breach of trust, the vulnerability of the child victim, the serious nature of the sexual act, the absence of remorse, and the need for deterrence, the prosecution respectfully urges this Honourable Court to impose a stern and exemplary sentence in accordance with section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017,” he said.

items.title: No whipping, 30 years’ jail for Filipino worker convicted of killing colleague in Kunak estate
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 20 — A palm oil transporter was sentenced to 30 years’ jail by the High Court after pleading guilty to murdering his female co-worker with a machete over personal dissatisfaction. Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos ordered Roger Pasague Cullano, 54, to serve his sentence from the date of his arrest on June 14, 2025, and to be referred to the Malaysian Immigration Department upon completion of his prison term. Roger was spared whipping due to his age.

items.title: MPOB probes alleged palm oil blending, relabelling at Port Klang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) is investigating a complaint alleging the blending of imported cooking oil with local supplies, and the relabelling of products for export as Malaysian products. MPOB said the blending of palm oil and palm-based products is part of the industry’s processing activities, subject to compliance with licensing conditions, quality standards and the applicable legal provisions. “The determination of the country of origin of export products must comply with the applicable Rules of Origin, including product-specific criteria under the relevant trade agreements.

items.title: Court of Appeal restores death sentence for man convicted of sodomising and murdering nine-month-old baby
items.summary: Court of Appeal judge Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz said the actions of the respondent, Mohamed Badruldin Mohamed, 41, demonstrated a blatant disregard for responsibility and a profound betrayal of the trust placed in his family. The sentence of 30 years’ imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court is set aside and replaced with the death sentence by hanging for the murder offence under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” she said when delivering the court’s decision. In the judgment, Hayatul Akmal said the sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court was inadequate.

items.title: Perlis NGO director arrested at KLIA2 over alleged RM85,468 criminal breach of trust
items.summary: KANGAR, Nov 20 — The director of a non-governmental organisation (NGO) based here was arrested by police on suspicion of committing criminal breach of trust involving funds belonging to the organisation amounting to RM85,468 in Sepang, Selangor today. Perlis Police Chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the 31-year-old man was detained by police from the Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Perlis Contingent Police Headquarters, at the domestic arrival gate of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 (KLIA2) at 11.05am today following information and intelligence. He said police will not compromise on any form of criminal breach of trust involving the abuse of position, power, and trust given, adding that firm action will be taken against any party found involved in unlawful activities regardless of the individual’s position or status.

items.title: Nuclear plant in Selangor? State scouting coast from Kuala Langat to Sabak Bernam, but nothing final yet
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — Selangor is looking at sites along its coastline, from Kuala Langat to Sabak Bernam, for a proposed nuclear power plant, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today. Amirudin was responding to Pakatan Harapan assemblyman for Kota Damansara Muhammad Izuan Ahmad Kasim, who asked about the state’s nuclear energy plans, including the proposed allocation and potential sites, at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting here. Amirudin said the Selangor Nuclear Council, made up of academics and industry players, was drawing up a roadmap to prepare the state for developing a nuclear industry, The Star reported.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB acknowledges mistakes, reaffirms loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today pledged allegiance to Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and vowed to uphold the sovereignty of the state’s royal institution, abide by the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 and comply with all decisions of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU). Ismail said the undertaking reaffirmed his recognition of Tuanku Muhriz as the state’s legitimate Ruler and his commitment to safeguarding His Royal Highness’s sovereignty, powers, rights and privileges. I therefore affirm unequivocally that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the legitimate Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Putrajaya’s plan for Rohingya refugees: Train 10,000 in skills, resettle them in Türkiye
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Cabinet has agreed to resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees from Malaysia in Türkiye through a structured skills training programme, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today. Zahid said the refugees would undergo a Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme lasting three to six months, focusing on practical skills in demand among employers across various industries in Türkiye. Zahid said Putrajaya would work with Turkish authorities, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and relevant agencies to coordinate participant selection, training, documentation and resettlement.

items.title: Anwar says pressure won’t change his support for Xi Jinping or China ties
items.summary: SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had no regrets about giving his full support to Chinese President Xi Jinping despite various pressures, reaffirming Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with China. Anwar said his support was based on his confidence in Xi’s leadership, particularly his ability to bring major world powers together and foster peace amid geopolitical uncertainties. Anwar also commended Xi for bringing together United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, describing it as an achievement few world leaders could accomplish.

items.title: Anwar says Xi’s interest in Malaysia Madani reflects China’s openness to deeper cultural ties
items.summary: SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he was struck by Chinese President Xi Jinping’s keen interest in the Malaysia Madani concept and efforts to deepen understanding between Islamic and Confucian civilisations, describing such attention from the leader of a major power as rare in bilateral relations. Anwar said Xi’s attention to these matters was among the highlights of their bilateral meeting today, reflecting China’s openness to Malaysia’s perspectives on Madani and inter-civilisational cooperation. Anwar said Xi had previously expressed interest in strengthening cooperation in these areas through dialogue, research and initiatives to promote mutual understanding between Islamic and Confucian civilisations.

items.title: Not so fast: Negeri Sembilan palace says Ismail Lasim must show majority support, not just deny resigning as MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace today said Datuk Ismail Lasim must show that he still commands majority support in the state assembly and submit a list of state executive councillors, after he denied resigning as menteri besar. The palace was responding after Ismail told reporters this morning that Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had instructed him to carry on, following reports that he had resigned in a letter dated November 16. The palace said Ismail must also submit a list of state executive council members for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration.

items.title: Maju Holdings boss, wife to face 21-day trial over RM458.5m CBT, money laundering charges from July 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Sessions Court today fixed 21 days between July and October next year for the trial of criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering cases involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife, Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi. Abu Sahid faces five charges of misappropriating more than RM458.5 million in company funds entrusted to him, involving bank accounts in Taman Tunku and Taman Serdang Perdana between May 3, 2016 and October 21, 2019. Noor Azrina, meanwhile, was charged with receiving proceeds from unlawful activities amounting to RM67.14 million through her bank account from Abu Sahid’s account.

items.title: Tawau house fire claims lives of two siblings aged 10 and 13
items.summary: Tawau Fire and Rescue Station chief Deputy Fire Superintendent II Jemishin Ujin said the department received an emergency call at 6.13am, with the first fire engine arriving nine minutes later. “Two victims were still trapped inside the house when firefighters arrived, prompting an immediate rescue operation. Jemishin said the fire destroyed about 70 per cent of the building.

items.title: Johor data centres’ water usage is just over 1pc of state’s treated water production, says exco
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 20 — The 19 data centres in Johor consume 21.277 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water, which makes up only 1.05 per cent of the state’s total treated water production, said State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh. He explained that the data centres had initially requested 73.088 MLD of water, but a lower volume of 21.277 MLD was approved instead, which makes up 3.35 per cent of the industrial sector’s total water consumption. “Another 11 data centres consume less than 1 MLD of water, while the remainder consume between 1 and 4.172 MLD.

items.title: Anwar meets Xi for fourth bilateral talks as Malaysia-China ties deepen
items.summary: SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today held a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, reaffirming close diplomatic ties between Malaysia and China. The 20-minute meeting was held at Qilin Villa State Guest House and is the fourth between Anwar and Xi, reflecting continued high-level engagements as Malaysia and China strengthen their strategic partnership. The third meeting took place on September 2, 2025, in Beijing, China.

items.title: Johor vows tougher action as school bullying cases climb past 1,000 a year
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 20 — The Johor state government will take more serious steps on the safety and well-being of students in schools, following a concerning number of recent bullying cases. He said official statistics from the Education Ministry showed an upward trend in bullying cases nationwide, rising from 6,528 cases in 2023 to 7,681 cases in 2024. “In Johor, 984 bullying cases were recorded in 2023, increasing to 1,080 cases in 2024.

items.title: No plans to resume use of the automatic number plate recognition system for now, says Penang exco
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 20 — Penang has no immediate plans to resume using its automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) system, state executive councillor H’ng Mooi Lye said today. However, H’ng said there is no set date for when both city councils will resume using the system. “We will definitely announce to the public if we resume using the system, even if it’s for parking management and data collection,” he said.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz decrees Ismail Lasim to stay on as Negeri Sembilan MB; Ismail says he never submitted resignation letter
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Datuk Ismail Lasim will remain Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on the decree of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, amid controversy over a purported resignation letter that Ismail denied submitting or authorising. Ismail said Tuanku Muhriz had instructed him to continue carrying out his duties to ensure continuity in the state administration. “I wish to clarify reports concerning a letter of resignation as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar dated Nov 16.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan impasse: Ismail Lasim granted audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 10.17 am today for an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, amid the administrative impasse in the state. Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz arrived at the palace at about 9.30 am, followed by three Undang Luak (traditional chieftains) of Negeri Sembilan. They were Rembau Undang Luak Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Sungai Ujong Undang Luak Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Jelebu Undang Luak Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.

items.title: Declassified minutes show Hannah Yeoh objected to Najib house arrest, says Lim Guan Eng
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today defended Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh over her role in the pardon process involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, saying she had upheld the party’s opposition to Najib’s house arrest proposal during a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting. Lim said declassified minutes from the September 18, 2026 Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting showed that Yeoh had clearly stated her objections to the move during proceedings chaired by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. He said that despite her objections, Yeoh had complied with a royal decree requiring her to sign the pardon proclamation.

items.title: Residents’ association cannot force homeowners to become members, Shah Alam court rules
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A residents’ association cannot automatically make homeowners its members or compel them to pay security fees backdated over previous years, the Sessions Court here has ruled, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. The case centred on the association’s position that Abdul Farid was automatically a member and owed security charges going back to 2013. Abdul Farid maintained that he had never applied for membership.
